newsitem.title: USA: World Bank sees rising Latam GDP, lower inflation.
newsitem.headline: World Bank sees rising Latam GDP, lower inflation.

text.p: The World Bank's Latin America lead economists expect the region's gross domestic product to rise and inflation to fall over the next two years, according to working numbers released Wednesday.

A set of tables handed out at a press briefing on the fringes of the IMF/World Bank annual meeting showed Latin America's GDP-weighted mean real growth would be around 2.7 percent in 1996, 4.1 percent in 1997 and 4.6 percent in 1998.

Another set of tables of projections for annual changes in consumer price indices showed that the region's GDP-weighted inflation rate is likely to decline from 18.6 percent in 1996 to 11.4 percent in 1997 and 4.3 percent in 1998.
World Bank authorities stressed that these were not official forecasts but rather their experts' best estimates of likely performance.
In 1995, the year of the Mexican peso crisis, Latin America's GDP grew by a disappointing 0.7 percent, down from 4.9 percent in 1994, its best year in more than one decade.
Despite that setback, inflation decrease last year, ending at 25 percent, against 348.5 percent for 1994.
